## Details

### elekloader

Mod loader: user supplies the stock OS file, the tool builds the custom .syx locally. Device table in the README (3016dca, 2026-11-08): Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1/Keys supported; Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.12 experimental; Octatrack 1.40C supported (linkable core boots on an MKII); Model:Cycles and Model:Samples 1.13 supported (builds work on both units); Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 supported; Analog Four MKII 1.56 experimental proof of concept (hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit). Canonical repo is unclear: the forum post also embeds github.com/elekloader/elekloader (web app at elekloader.github.io/elekloader); forks exist (AvroraPolnareff, naturarum, toonst, simonjohansson); none is listed, as none has changes of its own. Forum: builder issue reported 2026-10-19. Licence GPL-2.0-or-later. 2026-11-10 (8daa2ea): the shop's list, forms and bots moved to elekloader/shop (#338); mods are submitted there. machine-pages 1.8-1.10, machines-dn1 0.5/0.6 and machines-dn2 0.5 add mono machines and MIDI CCs (emulator-tested per TESTS.md). The linker now refuses odd jump targets into mod RAM after a Digitakt II froze at boot (I61). The README offers a Windows .exe; not every release carries the macOS .dmg. 2026-11-10 (main): core-ar2 0.13 opens the Rytm MKII's TEST slots 44-52 to mod machines, adds per-voice trig and velocity getters, screen calls through stock's routines and per-mod knob ids; machine-pages 1.7 tagged. 2026-11-12 (main): core-a4mk2 0.6 brings core-ar2 0.10-0.13's foundations to the Analog Four MKII (field defaults, the modified mark, the project-save event, payloads, knob looks, screen calls) and a 37.7 MB mods' area. Builds pick older core or helper versions by themselves when a mod patches a place a newer one took (Tone+FX's Digitakt files and Digi EQ 1.0c link with DT1 core 4.0 only; OB-1 0.6 with machine-pages 1.2), and released versions stay available while a listed mod needs them. 2026-11-13 (main): a third file family, ELE2, for the Analog Rytm MKI OS 1.74 (Modwerk's Rytm MKI research holds the measurements behind the profile); the README's table also names 1.73, the profile only 1.74. core-ot 0.9-0.40 opens about 40 more Octatrack events and tables to mods (mutes, sequencer moments, LFO waves, popup rows, PATTERN SETTINGS and PERSONALIZE rows, the playback increment, card file calls, the engine task's jobs, a block to DSP core 1). 2026-11-15 (FORMAT, SDK, CORES): std1 'standard events': a mod that sets events std1 subscribes to device- neutral event names, each core maps them to its own tables, and a subscription the core does not map is refused at link time; std1 and native mods link in one build. core-a4mk2 0.7 is the first core with it and adds native A4 events for knob turns, the analog voice frame and modulation edits. A frame-check build that copied one voice's analog frame words over another's silenced track 1 and was fixed in 0.3 (unit or emulator not stated). 2026-11-16 (docs/CORES.md, DRIVE.md, FORMAT.md, core-dn1 README): on the Digitone mk1 the build descriptor now carries the stock bytes of each flashed range (ABI 1.2), and TELOS's linker refuses a +Drive mod site that is not stock on the unit, overlaps the flashed build or another mod, or a region outside a free area (link codes 21-28). core-dn1 5.4's core_stock_info copies the OS image to 0x44200000 before the OS runs. 2026-11-17 (ADAPTING, FORMAT, core-ot, settings-ot, dspload-ot, core-a4mk2 READMEs): core-ot 0.41/0.42 add 16 Octatrack events (tempo, scenes, card mount and USB DISK MODE, previews, recorder commands, pages, track select, windows, crossfader, pattern select and edits, arrangement); new dspload-ot 0.2 sends DSP code at run time (mod.json `dsp_load`), also for TELOS card mods; refusal code 23 `early` for a site the OS ran before the +Drive or card link. On the Analog Four MKII the lock service is now checked on a unit. 2026-11-18 (v0.11.0, docs/DRIVE.md, CORES.md, drive-loader-a4mk2 and drive-loader-ar2 READMEs): v0.11.0 ships the newest core of every device, core-a4mk2 0.9 included. The Analog Four MKII gets its own +Drive mods loader (drive-loader-a4mk2 0.1, not yet run): stock 1.56 keeps the +Drive as raw sectors with no file system, so the loader keeps its own two-copy store in sectors stock never addresses. The Rytm loader (0.6) now reads each file into the +Drive area itself (a 64 KB floor replaces the 512 KB staging buffer), and +Drive mods may hold storage fields, sites over the OS, claims, tables of their own, knob ids and std1 subscriptions where the build's descriptor flags allow (descriptor ABI 1.3). drive-loader-ar2's README asks for core-ar2 0.14 while core-ar2's mod.json at the tag reads 0.13. New A4 MKII check mods for live recording, the sequencer and moments (read as expected in the emulator, 2026-11-14). 2026-11-20 (ADAPTING, CORES, DRIVE, FORMAT; core-ar2 README and SKIPS.md; core-dt2, core-dn2, core-a4mk2, drive-loader, smpl-machines READMEs; new AR2 and DT2 examples): core-dt2 1.1 keeps mods' project and kit data in bytes stock writes as zeros (191 bytes a kit), adds value rows, a per-frame parameter event and key LEDs; core-dt2 1.2 and core-dn2 0.5 add what TELOS needs on the unit (card ready, project save and load, crash, restart, task list), checked in digikit's emulator only, not yet on a unit. core-ar2 0.15: knob faces, mod folders in the +Drive sample browser, pad strikes before stock and LED colours, a held USB input gain step, note ends, track mutes, DIN MIDI out, machines given slots by count; 0.16: four optional CPU skips, off at boot (silent voices, idle sample layer, the UI's dynamic_cast, idle delay and reverb), two of which change the sound slightly, and GLOBAL submenus. The linker hands out machine slots, page ids and mod-declared id pools by count, kept in the lockfile. New smpl-machines (a SMPL page machine layer) and smpl-knob-c. Five new Rytm check examples and kit-memo-dt2. core-a4mk2 0.10's core_project_keep lets the A4 loader's APPLY & RESTART keep unsaved project changes. core-a4mk2's README now says core 0.2's pages drew identically on a unit (OS 1.56). 2026-11-22 (AGENTS, ADAPTING, CORES, DRIVE; core-ar2, drive-loader-ar2 and drive-loader-a4mk2 READMEs and PAGE.md; five new Rytm check examples): core-ar2 0.17 brings the std1 standard events to the Analog Rytm MKII and adds knob flags: a mod's own knob can open a destination list as LFO DEST does (only the list bit is honoured). core-ar2 0.18 adds restart calls. drive-loader-ar2 now needs core-ar2 0.18, marks mods with saved data with * and has APPLY & RESTART, as the A4 loader. The new Rytm check examples (std, std-midi, ui, voice, knob-flags) are built and linked only. The core-ar2 README restates its OS-upgrade restart check: analog-emu hung on 5 of 15 upgrades without core's restart routine and 0 of 15 with it (0 of 30 with the panel link paced as on a unit). 2026-11-24 (docs/DRIVE.md, drive-loader READMEs): drive-loader-ar2 0.12 and drive-loader-a4mk2 0.2 give mods a versioned +Drive payload API (drive_payload_abi, count, at, find, info with id, length and sha256, dl_payload_read; imported weakly by sidecar-core) and lock a loaded mod's file until the next boot: an upload over it is kept as <name>.new and swapped in at the next boot with the new CRC written first, so a power cut cannot leave the new file under the old CRC; the MODS page shows UPDATE or LOST and refuses DELETE (IN USE: RESTART FIRST). On the A4 reads that span a card sector go straight into the caller's buffer (a 4 KB read takes 7-10 card reads, not 64-80). 2026-11-25: core-ar2 0.20 adds `ev_store_adopt` (a sound or kit saved with another layout or before core storage is handed to its mod once as it loads; example adopt-check-ar2) and mod storage fields can be pinned to fixed bits with `offset`. core-ar2 0.21 moves the Rytm MKII mods area to 0x47B48000-0x47FFF000 (4.7 MB), above stock 1.74 USB audio feedback ring at 0x47B47440-0x47B47480, which stock rewrites while a host has the audio alternate setting selected; 0.11-0.20 started at 0x47B10000 and reached that ring once a build passed 221 KB. 2026-11-26 (docs/ADAPTING.md, DRIVE.md, core-ar2 README and SKIPS.md, examples/drive-machine-check-ar2): core-ar2 0.22 lets +Drive mods add machines too: `core_machines` now spans all 19 hidden slots 34-52 (was 10, slots 34-43), and the Drive Loader's entries reach the machine table after `ev_boot_drive`, after which the project loads again (with 0.21 they never reached it). New example drive-machine-check-ar2 tests this without a +Drive. 2026-11-27 (docs/ADAPTING.md): the build profiles pin -std=gnu17, so a gcc that defaults to C23 (15 and later) builds the same code; a mod's own cflags may name another standard.

### elektron-firmware-tool

C, MIT licence. Unpacks Elektron .syx firmware and repacks it as a valid file. Lists Analog Heat MKI, MKII and +FX among supported devices - currently the only Analog Heat-relevant tool we found. Forum listing: 113 stars, repo created 2026-07-22, "last commit 1 month ago" at the time of listing.

### Overtone

Python 3.11+ patcher (patcher/patch.py) that builds Overtone from the user's own OS 1.12 and only saves the result if it matches the tested build byte for byte; install via Elektron Transfer over USB. Adds machines SOPHIE, MACHINEDRUM, LOOP, THRU, per-track insert effects, envelope followers, two arpeggiators, parameter slides and GROOVE (replaces swing). 1.0.1 fixes installing an OS sent with Transfer while Overtone runs. About 160 checks per build in two emulators (digikit for the main OS, a SHARC emulator for the DSP program); author states 1.0.1 passes all of them, is played on a Digitone II and Transfer installs were checked on the unit. Opening Overtone projects on stock OS is untested. Recovery section is detailed (FUNC + TRIG 4, DIN MIDI, ~15 min). AGPL-3.0-or-later (includes dnfw), 5 commits. Related: dnfw, digikit, dn2-cfw, Schwung Sophie (MIT), and the author's digitone-2-modding-skill used with Claude Code. 2026-11-17 (README, v1.6): arps, LFOs and followers also work on MIDI tracks to play and modulate external gear; a follower can listen to the main mix or the audio inputs; a trig with only locks now slides too. 2026-11-20 (README, v1.7/v1.8): the README now says Overtone 1.8 is played on a Digitone II and passes about 190 emulator checks per build (160 before); the patcher also stores the packer's choices (no OS bytes), so it rebuilds the tested file in seconds instead of 1 to 3 minutes. 2026-11-22 (README, v1.9): GROOVE's presets are now listed with their step weights (the SW presets reproduce Elektron's SWING 54-71 %, and any swing value can be typed in as two weights); unlike Elektron's swing, GROOVE moves every step, the arpeggiators and micro timing. GROOVE now also works while the Digitone follows external MIDI clock; early steps play ahead of their clock from the measured tempo and can sit slightly off in the first beat after PLAY. The README says 1.9 passes every check (about 190) and installs and boots on a Digitone II, but its GROOVE changes are not yet played on a unit (1.8 was). 2026-11-23 (README rewrite, v1.10 commit message): v1.10 adds arp modes SHUF (held notes over RANGE in one random order, redrawn on each trig or chord) and RAND (a random note and octave each step) on both arps. ARP 2 runs while a track key is held with the sequencer stopped, gains RANGE (x1-x8) and SLIDE, and has no TRUE mode. Fixed: FREE mode and the 1/128 speeds were lost when a sound loaded. At the tag the README said 1.10 installs and boots on a unit and SHUF/RAND were played there; the shorter README now omits this. 2026-11-25: v1.11-v1.13. MACHINEDRUM is polyphonic (each voice its own engine) and takes unison; picking it switches the track unison off. SETTINGS > SYSTEM > LIVE KNOBS OFF makes knobs show stored values as on stock (kept over power cycles). v1.11 fixed crackles on MACHINEDRUM P-I models when many notes or unison voices started at once (altstrument notes). TRK + PLAY, PARAMETER + NO and FUNC + COPY/PASTE/CLEAR in the arp menus now cover Overtone parameters. 2026-11-27 (README, tags v1.14 and v1.15): undo and redo with [-] and [+] (not in KEYBOARD mode) over up to 50 steps of what a pattern save would store, pattern and kit, grouped by a pause of about two seconds; changing the pattern starts a new history. Arp speed NOTE moves the arp one step per trig or key (ARP 1) or per note played (ARP 2), restarting at PLAY/STOP. MACHINEDRUM voice management now fades out the quietest voice when a new note needs room, and while the DSP is busy it cuts only inaudible tails unless the load passes 90 %. The README makes no new statement about unit tests of these versions.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument: v1.1 (2026-10-30) reworks GROOVE with presets, a random drift control, random weights and arrow-key editing, and restores FUNC + TEMPO as tap tempo; v1.0.1 (2026-10-29) fixes installing Elektron's OS or an Overtone update with Transfer while Overtone runs._

### x0x (808/909 kick machines)

808 and 909 kick machines (MODEL 0 = 808, 127 = 909; TNTUN, DECAY, ATTK) that use the device's own sequencer, filters, AMP and effects, built from the user's stock OS for each device. On the Digitone II a new kick fades the previous one on the same track over about 2.7 ms. Physical qualification on Digitakt and Digitone is in progress (issue 94). docs/dn2-remote-control.md drives a DN2 1.12 remotely through a DigiHealth helper (remote keys, screen frames, ColdFire and DSP peek). Licence file not found in the clone. Found by GitHub code search 2026-11-03.

### SYXGRID v2

Free browser-based pattern/sequence editor, not a firmware mod. Repo includes sysexmap/, a public reverse-engineered SysEx format map (CC BY 4.0): 45 mappings, map version 1.13.0, each with a confidence level (A = hardware-confirmed on a DN2: 23; B = corpus-confirmed by repo fixtures: 12; C = inherited, one value exercised: 9; D = unknown, do not rely: 1). Narrowed by bisection on 2026-09-08 against a Digitone II (OS 1.10E) and a Digitakt II. Not decoded: parameter locks, sound parameters (filter, amp, FX, LFO), synth machine choice. Needs the DN2 in SYSEX RECEIVE mode; Web MIDI needs Chromium over HTTPS or localhost (Chrome/Edge 152 break SysEx receive on macOS). App is AGPLv3 since v22.46 (MIT through v22.37). 6 commits.

### DN2 DT2 firmware research

Source-only recipes for Digitone II firmware with six Digitakt II sample machines (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE), stereo samples, sample browsing, DT2 parameter graphics and SLICES trig mode. Recorder adds recording/resampling, source selection, normalization, trimming, audition, saving to +Drive and optional track assignment; VOICE cycles Voice Setup, Sample Manager and Recorder. Class-compliant USB audio provides 42 capture channels at 48 kHz/24 bit (MAIN, tracks 1-16, DELAY, REVERB, CHORUS, INPUT as stereo pairs) and a stereo return. R012 needs only the official DN2 1.11 and DT2 1.16 OS files; silent compatibility data replaces the private sample bank, and users load their own playable samples afterward. Native and browser builders verify exact inputs and the output: 2,563,872 bytes, SHA-256 4a2742a4...63a3a9a. The browser builds locally without uploading files; neither builder flashes the instrument. No firmware images or samples are distributed. Historical exact T1E2/R003/R008/R011 builds still require their original private sample bank. R011 fixed USB publication stalling after project changes by selecting its candidate destination from current DMA START while preserving ownership checks; R012 retains that fix. Owner-confirmed stock audio, samples, Recorder and USB audio on R012, including after project changes. Stable does not mean exhaustive validation: exact trimmed-file comparison, full Recorder-source coverage, endurance and end-to-end USB latency remain unverified. Builds on dnfw (angellinares/dn2_firmware_explore), selache, digikit and elektron-firmware-tool. AGPL-3.0-or-later. 2026-11-03: README warns new users NOT to install R012 yet. R012 mounts an existing sample filesystem but does not create one on a DN2 that never had it; symptoms are 0% Free / 0 bytes in Transfer, stalled uploads, Connection failed. The author says stock FORMAT +DRIVE, EMPTY RESET and FACTORY RESET do not create it and can erase projects; at that point an on-device formatter was still in development. R013 subsequently added FORMAT SAMPLES with erase confirmation; formatting, restart, capacity and post-format uploads were checked on the owner's unit. Owner testing of R012 had used storage prepared during development. An earlier track-2 saved-project reload report was an unsaved checkpoint; R022 addresses a separate, reproduced failure to refresh the sample table in the unsaved working-state backup. This does not establish recovery from an interrupted write or USB freeze.

### digikit

Native Rust emulator that runs the ColdFire and SHARC+ firmware together, with front panel, display and audio, plus a web panel (WASM core), a Tauri desktop app, the patch toolchain "patchkit" (applies modules to the user's own .syx), a headless scenario runner with pinned PCM hashes, a control socket for patch injection and DSP/ColdFire analysis databases with Ghidra tooling. README caveats: the DSP "does not run in real time yet", the browser host is parked on branch wip/browser-host, "no patched firmware has been installed on a device", and recovery via the bootstrap menu is "not tested on hardware". patchkit refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8. 2026-11-12 (b657f37, via altstrument): a USB take-over for fast sample transfer in the workbench with a read-back hash check per file, a diagnostic module that reads card information, a restructured SDK, fixes to the card image and the patch kit on Windows. 982 commits, AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra section-7 terms (attribution, origin, names) in NOTICE; page shows 46 open issues. GitHub marks it as not a fork. The org ElekLabs has 2 public repos: digikit and a fork of js216/selache. Original author: the GitHub profile m-dwyer is named "Em D" (Melbourne), which is exactly the credit ElekLabs' NOTICE requires ("digikit by Em D"); Overtone credits digikit to "Em D" as well. The earlier repo m-dwyer/digikit (196 commits, 4 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later, README at the time: "no audio", last visible file HANDOVER-2026-09-16) shows no move/archive notice and does not mention ElekLabs. ElekLabs has no public members, so the pages themselves do not show who runs it; the maintainer (user of this repo) states that Em D develops in ElekLabs/digikit (2026-10-31, not verifiable on the pages). The licence changed from GPL-2.0-or-later to AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra terms. Treat both repos as one project line, ElekLabs/digikit being the current one. Mod READMEs that say "digikit's emulator" mean this project. 2026-11-14 (finding 123 rewritten, findings 128-129, docs/MODULES.md, docs/ADDRMAP.md): the USB take-over is deleted (its commands answer E_STATE); core/usb-bulk-audio adds a vendor bulk OUT interface to the USB AUDIO/MIDI configuration at boot, so there is no mode switch (a probe sent 200 MB at 28 MB/s while audio played; real uploads 3.38 MB/s on a DN2, 2.74 MB/s on a DT2). Runtime 0.7.0: modules declare machines and effects with builder calls and the runtime commits them at once or refuses; a module of another major.minor is refused (E_CONTRACT); the patched-in content macros are gone. An address map names code addresses in crash records and profiles; the debug module can keep a card log that survives a crash. Finding 128 (static): the SHARC hook sites cannot move into run-time services, because the ColdFire uploads the whole DSP image before the card is readable. 2026-11-15 (MODULE-AUTHORING, design/module-sdk, handover): modules no longer declare their DSP cycles; module:check measures the worst steady block and stores a per-voice or per-effect DSP cost in the package, and one shared rule (largest voice cost x voices + effect costs within the headroom) now runs in the boot planner, the menu, patchkit fit and the web Transfer tab, which refuses a selection over the limit ('DSP LOAD need > free'). Modules built for the old descriptor must be rebuilt. Runtime limits now listed: 512 KiB arena, 64 KiB per module, 8 machine rows, 3 FX slots, DSP area 512 KiB (DT2) / 320 KiB (DN2). The SDK sample kernel has since landed (2026-11-16): the Shot machine fell from about 5,000 to about 2,450 (DT2) / 2,660 (DN2) emulator instructions a block, bit-identical. 2026-11-16 (findings 130 and 132, sdk/dsp/REGISTERS.md, handovers; runtime 0.8.2, untagged): one generated DSP register contract for module code (clobber, keep, stack, never_write), checked by patchkit build but only as a warning so far; the fx, machines, samples and lfo services are separate crates, the step before loadable services; module DSP tests moved to a SHARC-only rig (about 45 s instead of about 21 min). Finding 103 was partly withdrawn: several values reported as measured on silicon came from probe instructions the old assembler had mis-encoded (see digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md). No new unit run in this period. 2026-11-17 (findings 133-135, plans usb-fast-batch, runtime-slimming, r12-8-sharc-stubs, digikit-hot-reload, handovers; runtime 0.8.3, untagged): a Fast USB speed round ran on a DN2 (OS 1.12) and a DT2 (OS 1.17) on 2026-11-16 with every file hash-checked: one store-table commit for up to 16 files, copy/write overlap and fewer +Drive steps per file took a sample pack from 2.42 to 3.56 MB/s (DN2) and 2.32 to 3.07 MB/s (DT2) and a 9.8 MB file to 4.37 / 4.13 MB/s; a cached USB receive was slower and was dropped. Finding 133 (static): the card takes one transfer at a time under global mutexes, so parallel writers cannot help. Services become separate .dks files bound to the user's own firmware at install (patchkit bind; bound files hold firmware bytes and are never committed): lfo.dks is merged, Transfer installs the services a module needs (both emulator-tested), fx.dks and machines.dks are on a branch. Hot reload is an active plan again (finding 135, static firmware facts), not built. Facts in devices/digitakt-2.md. 2026-11-18 (findings 136-141, devices/syntakt.toml, plan syntakt.md): Syntakt OS 1.42 support in the emulator only. The emulator runs MAIN and the second ColdFire (section 7) in lock step, with digital audio (analog tracks silent); patchkit builds a no-seal 1.42 image that changes only section 3 and refuses sections 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 and 8; the runtime, menu, health and input adapters boot on the emulated 1.42 and load the debug module over emulated USB MIDI. Nothing has been flashed to a Syntakt. The DT2 and DN2 device files gained [protect] windows (hardware blocks a content module may not address; the packer refuses such a module) and [container] roles; the bulk OUT interface (core/usb-bulk-audio) is now in the default device image of both. 2026-11-18 (docs/PATCHING, MODULES, ARCHITECTURE, plans runtime-and-services and r12-8-sharc-stubs, port files): machines and effects are run-time modules only; patchkit now refuses a patch-time machine or effect row. The services machines.dks and fx.dks have landed: unbound files hold no firmware bytes, `patchkit bind` makes the stock tails from the user's own firmware, and Transfer installs the services a module needs (emulator example on DN2 1.12: machines.dks 29,718 bytes). The SHARC hook sites now jump through 16 slot words that a service fills (4 used). core/usb-bulk-audio (Fast USB beside USB audio) moved from a separate patch set into the default `device` and `device-introblank` sets on both devices. `patchkit pack` refuses a content module whose code or data holds an address inside a device's protected windows (flash controller, FPGA, peer buses). The DN2 OS 1.11 port file grew from 277 to 358 anchors (1.12: 359), adding the USB, card-driver, DSP voice and link anchors. No new unit run in these files. 2026-11-18 (findings 147-149, handover 2026-11-18, plans extension-model and port-file, MODULES, LFO module docs): runtime 0.9.0 refuses modules built for an older minor runtime version and duplicate keys in a boot selection; a new module kind lfo-shape (template and a first module, lfo_shapes_1, with seven 32-sample shapes; the service holds up to eight, as wave numbers 7 and up) and a core/lfo image adapter in every DT2 and DN2 patch set; content modules reload without a boot (refused while the transport plays); one port file per device and firmware, picked by the firmware hash, is planned. Findings 147-149 read the play state, the filter type and the LFO paths statically on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12. All emulator or static; no new unit run. An open risk the plan lists: after the last SysEx block the workbench flash flow can report done while the unit still writes flash. 2026-11-20 (finding 150 new, findings 110 and 148 updated, device files, plans and design digikit-project, extension-model, INSTRUMENTATION): the module file limit (upload stage buffer) doubles to 128 KiB on DT2, DN2 and Syntakt. Finding 150 reads the stock machine and filter type setters and the KitActive wrapper the machine chooser calls; finding 110 adds checked hook sites for a planned project service (slot setter, save, save exit) and what each stock project path (new, delete, clear, paste, format, load, rename) does; finding 148 traces the SHARC filter dispatch (two jump tables bounded at 7). The planned project service keeps per-project digikit data in projects/<slot>-<name>.dkp files, written after a successful stock save and archived, never deleted, when a slot changes hands. A calibration fit turns emulator instruction counts into device cycles from paired profiles. All static or emulator; no new unit run. 2026-11-21 (findings 151-157, plans card-write-guard, track-manager, usb-winusb, syntakt "Hardware bring-up", PATCHING "Flashing a Syntakt"): Syntakt hardware sets. The patched 1.42 image was 32 KB over the 2 MiB upgrade limit, so a core adapter (peer-image) stores the second CPU's section 7 packed and unpacks and hash-checks it in MAIN before it is streamed; a `device-peer` image with only that adapter and the full `device` set boot on the maintainer's unit. The first full image hung at the logo because the Syntakt bootstrap stages MAIN at 0x40200000 (DT2/DN2 0x40400000) and its in-place unpack overran (I183); patchkit now keeps an 8 KiB margin and refuses less. DIGIKIT > MODULES froze the unit because core/ui used Digitakt II key ids (I181); the first store lay beyond the unit's 1.82 GiB card (I182) and is now fixed at 1-1.5 GiB, checked against the driver's capacity. A new adapter card-guard hooks the firmware's eMMC write and erase and refuses requests outside each writer's sectors (on for the Syntakt, emulator-tested), against a stock Data API write that trusts the host's size (SB35). Also: a key-event hook site and the stock View and NameView classes (finding 155) with a planned shortcuts service and a track-manager tool module (host tests only); a WinUSB descriptor hook for the Fast USB interface (built, not yet tested on Windows or a unit); a DN2 unit calibration showing device/emulator SHARC cost factors from 1.01 (ALU) to 2.69 (memory). The public site still does not offer the Syntakt. 2026-11-22 (finding 158, FINDINGS, plans runtime-contract-and-lifecycle and ledgers/device-test-inventory, PATCHING, TESTING, AGENTS): the repository was reorganised (runtime/, services/, image-modules/, ports/; content modules under modules/<kind>/<author>/<name>) and checked byte for byte with a manifest tool. Finding 158, a static survey on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12 read once, says the ColdFire main OS runs from writable DDR, so almost every hook site and firmware table could be installed by the runtime at load instead of being flashed; the firmware has no indirect-call dispatcher to reuse; on the SHARC no load-time path exists, so 30 voice and effect sites stay flashed. A new plan (one package lifecycle for modules and services) follows from it. A new size gate measured the stored container against the 2,096,640-byte cap: DT2 1.17 1,616,928 B, DN2 1.12 2,028,608 B, Syntakt 1.42 2,102,528 B (5,888 B over; the first planned fix loads the DIGIKIT menu from the card). An inventory lists 105 device-test files that run on emulated units; a smoke set of 8 runs on each of DT2 and DN2. No new unit run. 2026-11-23 (finding 159 new, FINDINGS, plans resident-core-and-system-package, rc2s-1-boundary-inventory, rc3-header-table-v4, observability, runtime-contract-and-lifecycle, device files, ARCHITECTURE, TESTING): finding 159 (static) says the Syntakt image size is bound by the bootstrap's in-place unpack, so the stored literal tail of MAIN is padding, not waste, and no packer setting can beat it. The planned fix splits the runtime into a flashed resident core (about 108 KB) and a system package (about 167 KB) loaded from the card, with a new core-only level. The lfo service now installs its hooks at load; core/lfo left the DT2 and DN2 images. Header table v4 will refuse all older module files. No new unit run. 2026-11-24 (HEAD e3f877a): the DIGIKIT menu and the runtime lifecycle moved out of the flashed image into a card file digikit/system.dksp (system package, own 320 KiB block), installed by Workbench or patchkit after the flash; a flash alone boots core-only (no modules or menu; store and USB upload answer), as do 4 unstable boots in a row or a bad package; SysEx RETRY (0x0b) clears it. Package activation still needs a hardware check. Syntakt 1.42's image now fits with about 108 KB to spare (branch measurement). Modules can publish settings Workbench edits; new docs/FIRMWARE.md (per-release analysis databases for DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12, Syntakt 1.42); desktop Workbench gains patch-and-flash and flash-emulator flows. The Overdrive curves module was deleted. No new unit run. 2026-11-25 (RC4-4): the image points dynreg, params, machines and fxpages became one platform module, core/rows (`rows_info` replaces `dynreg_info`). Effect routes are picked in a stock-list row SETTINGS > FX ROUTING and apply without a restart (deferred to stop while playing); the MODULES list applies changes live. Service files can carry 1, 2 or 4 byte patches that are checked against the stock bytes before writing and restored in reverse order at unload. Runtime 0.13.0 adds per-service sections to the MODULES reply (caps bit 21); hosts refuse the older layout. Patch-time machine fixtures removed: every machine is a run-time .dkm. 2026-11-26 (HEAD de6f2a1; plan dsp-development-workflow, INSTRUMENTATION, MODULE-AUTHORING, sdk/dsp, debug module): image-modules/ is gone; the DSP slots dsp-voice, fx and dynfx moved to runtime/platform. A DSP workflow for module authors: offline rig renders with WAV/JSON compare, per-block profiles, Workbench sessions (a private emulator card plus captures). The debug module gained opt-in observers for the firmware's view stack (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) and for live parameter words (DT2 1.17 only). A stock-Delay reference case ran on the emulator and on a physical DT2 (OS 1.17, runtime 0.13.2 development image with the debug module): echo spacing 64.05 ms emulated against 62.49 ms on the unit, decay per repeat within 0.0011 dB. FREQ SHIFT gained SPREAD, DRIFT, RATE and FDBK (rig and emulator only). 2026-11-27 (new finding 131, findings 07/19/71, TESTING, MODULE-AUTHORING, ports/fw README, new dkglyph tool and glyph STYLE.md): finding 131 maps the Digitone II 1.12 MACHINE SEL rows (groups, dividers, keys) and a stock cursor fault after a SYN/FLTR page change (SB43). A settings page can now be built from a table of fields using the stock choice popup, and SETTINGS rows appear and go after a live load or unload without a project change. A service with a hook in interrupt context (lfo) is refused a live reload and needs a restart, after an lfo reload's unload step never returned on the Digitone II (cause not found). The Rust emulator now delivers forced interrupts by default. New glyph tool for 1-bit icons and animated value glyphs, with the stock screen measures written down; not yet drawn on a device. 2026-11-28 (new lfo-table, Ascend and Project manager READMEs, module-distribution plan, services/lfo, ports/fw, device files, design notes dkm and project, MODULE-AUTHORING, INSTRUMENTATION): runtime 0.13.6. A new platform module core/lfo-table is in every DT2 and DN2 patch set and adds LFO waves 7-14 by copying the four 7-entry wave tables and repointing their lea operands; the lfo service no longer hooks the LFO interrupt and fills the table from the UI task under the interrupt mask, after the 2026-11-27 reload hang. Modules can publish typed settings and answer read-only queries from a Workbench page (149 B request, 870 B reply, one at a time). A new .dkm header tag (PAYLOADS) is refused by older runtimes. New LIFECYCLE and STATE_CARRIED log events show where a boot, load or reload hangs. The distribution plan keeps firmware patching in the browser and installs only built module files. All host or emulator only.

### dn2_firmware_explore

Tools to inspect, modify and rebuild Digitone firmware (dnfw, CLI and browser), plus 17 mods for Digitone II 1.11 (Waverider wavetable machine, LFO4, arp modes, LFO waves, FX destinations and others), each with a version and a changelog. The ~80% recovery-path stall once listed as open was the MIDI link, not the image (settled 2026-09-11). AGPL-3.0-or-later. The container tools also unpack and rebuild Digitone / Digitone Keys (MKI) OS files (tests use DN1 OS 1.42A; its container is unsigned), and its parameter search on DN1 images is "not yet reliable" per the CLI; there are no mods for the MKI (README and source read 2026-11-11). 2026-11-12 (docs/os-versions.md, issue #382): port to OS 1.12 under way: address maps by instruction anchors decided all 778 mod sites (594 same bytes, 184 relocated), the platform has a 1.12 spec and a 1.12 test image boots in the emulator; every mod is to get a 1.12 build beside its 1.11 build, 1.11 stays the default until all are ported. 2026-11-13 (docs/os-versions.md): stock 1.12 touched no RAM from 0x46700000 up in an emulator run, bootscreen moves to 0x467e8000 on 1.12, the heap arena moves +0x1000 on 1.12 (S22), and lfo4 builds for 1.12 in the emulator. 2026-11-16 (README, docs/sendloop.md, docs/mods-page.md): new mod sendloop rewrites the ColdFire loop that copies each 1,344-word DSP frame into the transfer buffer (4 instead of 7 instructions a word, one 32-bit write instead of two), about 4 points less main-processor load, confirmed on hardware on OS 1.11. Every build now gets a MODS page (SETTINGS > SYSTEM > MODS) that lists the OS, the build name, the tool's commit and each mod's version; its code and rows sit at 0x46798000. 2026-11-18 (README): the sendloop mod is now on by default in builds.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument: OS 1.11 target; includes the dnfw inspect/modify/rebuild tool, which also runs in the browser. Hardware-confirmed mods: lfo4, arpmodes, lfowaves, midiarp, layermidi, fxmod and the lfolength fix (2026-10-09, audio track). No GitHub releases - tags are work snapshots._

### dn2-cfw

Public lab notebook: notes, tools and new effects, no Elektron firmware included. Seven builds run on real hardware per README (EF01 renamed stock, FLG1 flanger replacing the chorus, FTD1 + one-head tape delay, DH01 core/hook bus with a MIDI test mod, FTN1 renamed screens, GT00 parameter table moved, GT01 + 17 hidden rows for the 3-band compressor); not yet on the unit: the 3-band compressor and a Space-Echo-style delay (fx/spaceecho.c). Rule of the author: "nothing counts as working until it has run on my unit". Getting started (README): macOS on Apple silicon (Linux likely for most), Python 3, the user's own Digitone_II_OS1_12.syx in elektron-firmware/, upstream tools cloned into vendor/ (VENDOR.md) - for digikit and elekloader the author's forks on branch dn2-1.12 (digikit: 1.12 support, audio clock, DIN MIDI, LEDs, live play; elekloader: Digitone II 1.12 profile and the core-dn2 hook bus), commands scripts/dn2-emu-112.sh all, scripts/dn2-live.sh, fx make test/renders, tools/brickcheck/brickcheck CANDIDATE.syx (12 checks, must pass before any flash). README gives no step-by-step flashing procedure. Docs: ROADMAP.md, HANDOFF.md (later entries supersede earlier), FIRMWARE.md (sha256s), VENDOR.md, docs/parameter-table-growth.md, notes/ (one report per task, claims marked [verified] or [inferred]), analysis/ (class hierarchy recovered from RTTI). 28 commits, GPL-2.0(-or-later). 2026-11-22 (HANDOFF, ROADMAP, README, notes/UF01-upstream-fit.md): the EEEM test build ran on the author's unit on 2026-11-17 ("works fine over 15min of building a track"). MRB, a morphing reverb, replaces the shelved spring reverb. Five more MRB combinations pass the brick checker (12/12) and the pack checks, with a worst DSP block of 51-59 % of the frame in sharcvm (the shipped CFTE: 62.8 %); they wait for unit tests before 0.4.0. Two combinations with the tape echo do not fit. UF01 checks Digiwerk on paper against upstream elekloader (core 0.4, machines-dn2 0.5 on OS 1.12): they clash at the same 7 core hook sites, in DSP L1 from 0x2dd600 and in the parameter-table rows from 321; nothing was built. The README and release notes now call Digiwerk a separate project that contributes to Modwerk.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): Renamed Digiwerk (altstrument; stock OS 1.12, GPL-2.0-or-later, notarized Mac patcher app). v0.1.0 (2026-10-26): Deja vu LFO waves and the Compressor + Flanger pack (build DJ01). v0.2.0 (2026-10-29): key-following LFO wave, one-cycle and half-cycle LFO modes, SHUF/RAND/TM arp modes (also on MIDI tracks), a tape echo, per-slot effect choice. v0.2.1 (2026-10-30): withdraws the six spring-reverb builds - the page says the CFES and EFTS builds stop the sound on a Digitone II - and removes the spring tile from the patcher; the other eight builds are unchanged. 2026-11-10 (R1.18, in progress): MRB, a light morphing reverb for the reverb slot, after a port of the author's Beads morph reverb that cost 87k-158k DSP instructions a block; MRB takes 19k-21k (stock reverb 14.6k). The test build EEEM (stock compressor, chorus and delay + MRB) also turns DSP faults into tones whose pitch names the fault; it waits for the author's unit. The spring reverb stays shelved after it lost the sound on the unit (I68)._

### Overwitch

Multitrack Overbridge audio on Linux. Supports Overbridge 2 devices incl. Analog Heat, Heat MKII and Heat +FX, Digitakt I/II, Digitone I/II/Keys, Syntakt. GPL-3.0, 671 commits. 2026-11-18 (README, docs/adding.md on main, no release yet): Overbridge 1 devices (Analog Four MKI, Analog Keys, Analog Rytm MKI) are supported with recent OS versions that speak the Overbridge 2 protocol (e.g. A4 MKI OS 1.56); only the Analog Four MKI is tested. Their track layout is set per device and can be written to the device from the GUI; their blocks hold 1 ms of audio (1-5 blocks, default 3).

### OpenBridge - Digitone II

A Linux (x86_64) implementation of Overbridge for the Digitone II, as a VST3 plugin (JUCE; the standalone app was dropped on 2026-11-12): 42 channels of USB audio out and 8 in with clock-drift compensation, every sound parameter of the 16 tracks readable and editable with DAW automation, a mixer, and a preset browser for kit presets and the +Drive library. The README first said it was written from an analysis of the Overbridge 2.26.10 installer and measurements on the device, with Elektron's artwork extracted at build time from the user's own installer; since 2026-11-12 it says neither, and the build needs no installer. Delay time shows as a raw value. Not affiliated with Elektron. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-12. 2026-11-25: 0.1.5 follows knob, mixer and mute changes made on the device and adds Total Recall: the Digitone project is copied into the DAW project (again on each DAW save, up to 10 s) and on reopening the user picks the plugin or the device state; Plugin State replaces the project loaded on the unit. The README now names OS 1.11 as the minimum (was 1.12).

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-12, README (2026-11-12), README v0.1.5 (2026-11-25)_

### DN2 mk2 Mod (dn2mk2-firmware)

Adds Digitakt II sample machines (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE) with sample browser and recorder, PERC (34 Machinedrum machines incl. TRX, EFM, GND, P-I), Monomachine voices (SID 6581, DPRO WAVE/DDRW/DENS, VO-6) and a CPU guard. Browser-based patcher builds from the user's own files ("nothing is uploaded") and saves only if the output sha256 matches a build that passed scripts/ship_gate.py. Hardware: README says verification is pending per version; FIRMWARE.md says nearly every v0.21-v0.33 entry was checked in emulators and "not seen on hardware yet". Main open problem: DSP time (heavy voices cut sound). Flashing a 1.12 unit takes it back to a 1.11 base, projects saved under the newer OS may not open. 1,491 commits, 8 stars, AGPL-3.0-or-later. FIRMWARE.md says built firmware is kept on the repo's `builds` branch (not main) - unlike most projects here, which only ship patchers; we link only to the repo and docs, not to builds. Withdrawn builds: v0.4-v0.7 (oversized image). v0.38 (2026-11-02): Direct Jump state kept in its own +Drive sector (0x6FF000); per-project sample lists at +Drive 0x6D0000-0x6E02FF, two checked copies each. Root cause of the silent new samples: the DSP plays a pool slot only below the directory's count, and live adds did not update the count. v0.39 (2026-11-03): recordings had kept only ~2 ms since v0.38 because the DSP recorder took words 2-4 of every new link command as source, channel and threshold, and v0.38 sent a check command at every take's start; now only the recorder's own commands set them. 2026-11-15: the first test build, v0.54-t1 STEREO, is announced as a GitHub pre-release on the owner's request and listed under TEST in the patcher, not as the latest. Testers are asked to check hard-panned stereo files on headphones, filters and overdrive on both sides, and a fifth voice falling back to the mono mix. Next: stereo comb filters and sends, and the stock NAME screen for sample names. 2026-11-16 (FIRMWARE.md, release notes v0.54-v0.56): each build passed its gate in the emulator (54-56 gate steps) and is cleared to flash; unit results for these three builds are not reported yet. A DDRW sound saved with BR above 0 sounds grittier from v0.56. 2026-11-17 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.57, docs/flex-pool.md): v0.57 FLEXMUTE is gated (56 gate steps) and cleared. It answers a tester's unit report on v0.55/v0.56: MUTE SRC muted the source as soon as a take existed, and some tracks could not be unmuted until a power cycle. Now the SRC track drops out only while a FLEX voice has its note on and is heard, and comes back about 0.2 s after the note ends; known issue: a long gap between FLEX notes un-mutes the source. FLEX takes still measure about 6 dB below their source (to be fixed). The v0.54-t1 STEREO test build was taken off the patcher's list because stereo samples do not play yet (altstrument, 2026-11-16). Planned next: microtonal scales in KB SETUP and a one-handed keyboard latch. 2026-11-18 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.58): v0.58 SCALES added two microtonal scales to KB SETUP (PR12, a 12-note just tuning laid out as Chromatic; PM12, its 7-note minor laid out as Aeolian), retuning each voice by cents above ROOT. It passed its 57-step gate but crashed a unit in a chord MODE and was pulled from the patcher on 2026-11-17; the code is reverted on main, a fix is on a branch. Withdrawn builds now: v0.4-v0.7 (oversized image), v0.58 (crash). Planned next: MON on the recorder, the Monomachine FM+ machines, a per-track 4-band EQ, arp scale lock and in-key transpose. 2026-11-19 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.60-v0.61, docs/microtuning.md): v0.59 adds the Monomachine FM+ machines and MON on the recorder; testers found the FM+ knobs on the wrong parameters (I157), fixed in v0.60 together with GRID's ALLOCATE SLICE RANDOM, whose NO had put the old locks back. v0.61 adds microtuning: 12 offsets in tenths of a cent above ROOT, applied voice by voice in the audio interrupt from a double-buffered snapshot, never through stock's scale tables (so v0.58's crash cannot return); SLICE and GRID tracks, MIDI tracks and MIDI out are never retuned. The tuning is saved per project in its own +Drive sectors (two copies at 0x6E0400 + 2p + c, region 0x6E0400-0x6E04FF), two seconds after the last change and before LOAD or NEW. Known issue: ERASE MOD DATA does not clear the tunings yet. Both builds are gated (CLEARED TO FLASH); no unit result yet. Planned next: the SLICE editor, then a per-track 4-band EQ and arp scale lock; DT2 presets are on hold. 2026-11-20 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.62-v0.63, docs/sampler.md, docs/kbhold.md): v0.62 SLICE answers user requests for EDIT SLICE POINTS (edits heard 0.2 s after the knobs rest without YES, a played note selects its slice, zoom down to 128 frames read from the +Drive, FUNC + START/END snaps to a zero crossing within 512 frames) and lets CREATE SLICE GRID jump 2/4/8/16/32/64 with FUNC + E. v0.63 FLEXLEVEL: on the owner's unit a single-track FLEX take needed GAIN +24 to match its source by ear, so +24 dB is now built in (tracks already boosted get 24 dB hotter; MAIN and IN takes are still quieter than heard); saving a FLEX buffer had normalised the very take still playing, now it is kept as recorded. Both gated (CLEARED TO FLASH). The firmware is nearly full: a keyboard HOLD (PTN + KEYBOARD, planned at UI level only) does not fit the 2 MiB image yet and the per-track EQ is dropped for now; arp scale lock is next. 2026-11-21 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.64-v0.67, docs/banks.md, docs/packer.md, docs/midiarp.md, docs/kbhold.md): v0.64 HOLD makes PTN + KEYBOARD a sustain pedal on all 16 tracks through stock's own MIDI CC 64 sustain, so held keys, MIDI in and the arp latch; it fit only after the start-up animation was cut to every other frame (291 bytes left). v0.65 BANKS spreads PROJECT RAM over banks A-D (508 slots, still one 400 MB pool, the bank kept in SAMP's free low byte, new +Drive regions per project); a tester measured v0.63's +24 dB FLEX gain 12 dB too high, so v0.65 uses +12 (I185); an optimal aPLib packer, checked against the bootstrap's own depacker, frees about 87 KB. v0.66 NXT: a slide with no SLEN lock now lasts until the track's next trig (old patterns change), FM+ DYN FUNC + turn jumps 1FRQ / 2FRQ to whole ratios, and FLEX takes of MAIN and IN are recorded unchanged and played +12 dB (a saved take plays 12 dB quieter). v0.67 MIDIARP merges upstream dnfw's MIDI-track arp. All four gated (CLEARED TO FLASH), no unit result yet. Planned next: arp scale lock and a voice/load guardrail; DT2 presets on hold. 2026-11-22 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.68-v0.69, docs/perform.md, docs/guardrail.md, ROADMAP): v0.68 shows each mod machine's icon and name in MACHINE SEL by changing two stock instructions. On v0.67 (pattern volume 100, compressor off) the owner found FLEX takes needed 12 dB more, so v0.68 builds in +24 dB again for track takes and also for MAIN and IN takes; a tester had measured that same +24 as 12 dB too loud (I185, O48). v0.69 PERFORM adds eight macros A-H, each an offset on top of the sound's value, LFOs and locks, with up to five track and parameter targets and a depth of -64..+63, saved per project in the mod's +Drive sectors; turning a macro is not recorded into patterns yet, and ERASE PROJECT does not clear the macros. v0.69's DSP limit gives every mod machine a weight measured on the SHARC runner, and MACHINE SEL refuses a machine that would take the kit past 320,000 cycles (roughly three VO-6, two DENS, seven PERC or eleven sample tracks); stock machines weigh nothing and older kits load as they are. Planned next: arp scale lock and in-key transpose, a Machinedrum/Monomachine engine rewrite, then a keyframe stretch. 2026-11-23 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.70, docs/inkey.md, THIRD-PARTY.md): v0.70 applies two upstream mods by w-winter (dn2-firmware-explore pull requests #212, #214, #278; AGPL-3.0) byte for byte as 25 edits plus two code chunks at 0x467A8000 and 0x467B8000; the arp toggle byte is 0x405CD8AF, the degree offset sits in bits 2..5 of a track's pattern byte +1187. Upstream reports both working on units (2026-10); here the gate checks the arp and degree notes in the ColdFire emulator, not the [+]/[-] keys. The PERFORM fix answers a user report on v0.69: macros wrote block t for track t, but the mirror's blocks are voices; each target now moves every voice the voice-to-track table (0x80005308) gives its track. A pattern with degrees saved on stock loses them. 2026-11-24 (v0.71, v0.72, docs/engine-rewrite.md): each arithmetic change is one constant that restores the original bit for bit; sounds are held against the Machinedrum's own output at 60 dB SNR, the feedback and resonant machines by level (1 dB) and octave bands (3 dB). VO-6's guardrail weight went to 41,000 (measured 39,404; four tracks dropped a voice in the stress test). The P-I drums are not lighter yet (their delay lines need a new memory layout). A track's FLEX take recorded on v0.68-v0.70 stays 18 dB hot. The README now lists FLEX, the FM+ machines and the sequencer features (PERFORM, Direct Jump, slides, keyboard HOLD, microtuning, MIDI-track arp, arp in key, in-key transpose) and ERASE MOD DATA. 2026-11-25: docs/os-versions.md measures OS 1.11 to 1.12 (build 40059 to 40062): bootstrap, updater, the SHARC blob and the Outbox 8 firmware are byte-identical, MAIN OS grows 4,096 bytes and is shifted after +0x48a86 (new main-output routing view). A port to 1.12 is ColdFire work only (about 385 patch sites move); `dnfw mods apply` refuses 1.12 today. Going back from 1.12 to 1.11 rewrites only MAIN OS (SAFETY.md). 2026-11-26 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.73-t1-v0.75, docs/os112-port.md, docs/dsp-cost.md, docs/flex-design.md): v0.73-t1 was a test build of v0.72 on stock OS 1.12 for Outbox 8 users. It is not rebuilt from source: a gated 1.11 image is moved onto 1.12 by a porter that translates every edit, address operand and RAM address on evidence from stock's own references and refuses what it cannot place (v0.72: 114 edits, 827 operands, 10 data pointers moved). The 1.12 gate caught a hook whose last byte matched stock's call and so kept a 1.11 target, and a constant the compiler had folded from two addresses. The build passed the full gate on 1.12 and still crashed a unit during the start-up animation; it was pulled the same day (2026-11-25). v0.74 LIVEREC fixes sequencer lag in live recording with 6-7 keys (slide locks were cleared in three passes per key, now one). v0.75 PILEVEL moves the P-I machines' per-block scratch from DDR into one shared 2 KB area in the DSP's L1 (bit-identical output; PI-SD and PI-RS -47 %) and scales a track's FLEX take by the track's LEVEL as (LEVEL/100)^2 (stock applies LEVEL after the buffer FLEX reads). 2026-11-27 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.76, CLAUDE.md): v0.76 starts a recorder trig's take one sequencer tick after the step changes, less 2 ms, because while the pattern plays a step's notes go out about one tick (1/6 of a step) after the step changes; takes now play back within about 2 ms of their step (I230), and users can set microtime back to 0. PERFORM macros move in a parameter's fine units, which removes zipper noise. Bug and feature reports now come from a Discord analyst into a private bench repo and are recorded as taken, deferred or declined. Still built for OS 1.11 only; the 1.12 build stays pulled until its start-up crash (I215) is found.

### digitone-2-modding-skill

Agent skill (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor; install with `npx skills add`) for developing Digitone II firmware mods: ColdFire MAIN OS patching in C, SHARC DSP audio code, verification in two emulators (digikit + a whole-DSP SHARC emulator), rebuild/re-sign/flash over USB. Encodes stock-firmware addresses, hook sites, the ColdFire-to-DSP frame format, free memory and "hardware rules the emulators cannot check, which each once silenced a real unit" - read on 2026-10-31 via SKILL.md and references/*.md (SKILL.md has 20 rules incl. whole 32-byte boot blocks, stock encodings only, no L2 above 0x200B0000, never read unwritten DDR, 2 MiB image / section 7 under 1 MiB, stop after two failed flashes; scripts include hwrules.py, shapecheck.py, encodecheck.py, bootblocks.py, sim.py/simc.py, cfmod.py, rpc_flash.py). Facts and rules are folded into hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md and hardware/common/agent-workflow.md. Note: tree pages are blocked for our fetcher by robots.txt; the blob pages were readable. Examples: double_time (sequencer clock hook), track_trim (-6 dB on track 1). Needs Python 3.11+, dnfw, m68k GCC, digikit. MIT (digikit-derived files GPL-2.0), 2 commits, 10 stars. Overtone was built with it. Closest existing relative of this repo's hardware/ folder.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument: main @ 84c8cd3 (2026-10-29), no tagged releases; brick-risk flag set ("flashing carries a known, documented risk of damaging the device")._

### coldfire-rs

Rust stack for ColdFire V4e (MCF5441x): toolchain (rustc_codegen_gcc + libgccjit for m68k-elf), runtime, PAC generated from an SVD, and an Embassy HAL (GPIO, PIT, INTC, eDMA, UART, DSPI, eSDHC eMMC block reads, SSI/I2S, USB OTG device mode). Not an emulator and not an Elektron mod: the README never mentions Elektron or digikit, the only link is the topic tag "digitakt". It is relevant here because digikit names the MCF54415 as the control CPU of Digitakt II (and the Digitone II is described as ColdFire too). Drivers were run on the author's own MCF54415 board. README: API is young and may change before 1.0. 33 commits, Apache-2.0 OR MIT. Same owner also has deluge-sdk (Synthstrom Deluge, out of scope). Org shows no public members; no relation to ElekLabs/Em D found.

_Sources: GitHub README, FirestormAudio profile page_

### digi-roll-studio

Native Rust desktop sequencer for Digitakt II, Digitone II and Analog Four, built from digi-roll. Writes to hardware: README recommends throwaway projects. Safe-write ceremony of five rules (re-read and back up the destination pattern first, OS build on an allowlist, user confirmation, change only needed bytes, read back and byte-compare). Gen-2 dump protocol (digis) vs gen-1 (Analog Four). +Drive file-write commands 0x57/0x58/0x59 hardware-verified for a single chunk only, not called by the app (writes above 16 KiB refused); 0x5A/0x5B/0x5C (move/copy/delete) not implemented. Protocol code ported from elk-herd (BSD-2, (c) mzero). Fixtures: 34 real .syx dumps. 124 commits, GPL-3.0-or-later. Not firmware modding. Windows/Linux write testing incomplete. 2026-11-24 (v0.6.0/v0.6.1): Drum Steps, a 16-step grid editor beside the piano roll (paint, erase, velocity drag, per-track playheads); Kit Builder (K), a track grid and preset browser with filters, revert per track or for all auditioned tracks, a recovery backup kept even when verification fails; A4 writes keep the destination pattern's kit and refuse a blank pattern whose kit reference is unset (I201). A contributed Syntakt p-lock map (OS 1.42) is merged but enables no Syntakt writes. Saving a whole kit to the +Drive is planned for DN2 only.

### digitone-syx-toolkit

Python CLI (+ Tkinter GUI) to capture, replay, diff and hex-view SysEx, and to generate Digitone II PATTERN .syx from an empty template. README (Japanese) says Digitone II only. Hardware-validated: pattern-wide mode, tracks 1-8, steps 1-128, normal trigs, pitch, velocity, length (inherit/explicit/INF), tempo/speed/total steps, import/send. Not supported: chords, track-default rewriting, condition/probability/micro timing/retrig, non-destructive editing. Length encoding per README: inherit = 0xFF, explicit INF = 0x7F, finite 0x00..0x7E. 47 commits, licence not shown.

_Sources: GitHub README, SYXGRID README_

### DNX

Browser tools (Web MIDI, Chromium only, nothing uploaded) for Digitone and Digitone II projects: Expander (each sound-locked Digitone 1 sound gets its own track on the Digitone II), Manager (move/copy/swap/clear/rename patterns across banks with undo; Insights: polymeter, PATTERN RESET cost, voice use), Library (browse/search/rename the 2,048 +Drive presets; wavetables need Digitone II with "Waverider" firmware), Backup (whole +Drive into one .dnx with a manifest; excludes global settings), Probe (read-only identification and traffic capture) and CLI commands (project, plan, convert, copy, rearrange, rename, track, rebuild, diff, sheet; dry run by default). Write safeguards: WRITE switch must be armed, copy of current contents saved first, every write read back and compared, destinations checked against a fresh listing, never writes the loaded project, never converts a DN2 preset to DN1; close Transfer and Overbridge first (shared MIDI ports). Formats: .dnprj (DN1) and .dn2prj (DN2) projects, sound banks .syx; payloads LZ4-compressed inside a ZIP; SysEx uses 8-in-7 MSB-first. Author discloses LLM use; AGPL-3.0-or-later, TypeScript, 15 stars, created 2026-09-07. Not firmware modding. Report button opens a prefilled GitHub issue. 2026-11-10 (docs/KNOWN-ISSUES): an unpaged LIST of a 256-entry table store came back cut at about 4 KB with garbage after entry 125; listings are now paged in 64s (HYPOTHESES H23). 2026-11-15 (docs/samples.md): the owner dropped the digikit runtime from DNX's builds on 2026-11-12; the sample store keeps digikit's card-store format (store v3) but the project's own firmware now writes it through a /samples route on the Data API (files in 524,288-byte parts, at most 64 MiB a file, each part read back from the card and checked by xxHash32; no read-back of a stored file, no rename or move in version 1). The id of a stored sample is the SHA-256 of the native file. 2026-11-16 (docs/samples.md): before 2026-11-16 a plan that moved a sound to a new path ran the upload first, which sent nothing, and then deleted the only copy; the old copy is now deleted just before the upload. Layout and token docs (UI only).

### Elektron Emu

Five VST3 plug-ins (Mac, Windows) that run each machine's real OS in an emulated CPU: Digitakt II, Syntakt, Analog Rytm MKII, Digitone II, Model:Cycles. Firmware not included; the user places the .syx from Elektron's site in a per-machine folder. +Drive emulated and persisted; WAV loading on DT2, Rytm and DN2. Digitone II's DSP is compiled locally on first open (needs a C compiler, else a slow interpreter that renders offline only). Caveats: Rytm analog voices/effects are a custom model that does not sound like the real machine; Syntakt analog tracks 9-12 missing; Mac builds unsigned. 2 commits, 19 stars, no licence stated. Personal project, not affiliated with Elektron (panel photos belong to Elektron).

_Sources: GitHub README, altstrument tools page_

### elkflash

### TERRAIN for Digitone II

Unofficial custom OS for the Digitone II that adds TERRAIN, a wave-terrain synth machine (module "terreno"), plus quality-of-life mods. Built in the browser from the user's own OS 1.12 file: a patch list copies bytes from the user's sections 3 and 7 and inserts the project's own, then checks the result's SHA-256 against the tested build and reruns Elektron's integrity checks before the download. Built with a patched digikit (40 parameters per machine, voice adapter, OS 1.12 anchors) and dnfw's container code; several mods are ported from dn2_firmware_explore. Some page glyphs were captured from the stock pages (to be replaced by calls to the firmware's own drawing). Uninstall by sending the original OS 1.12. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-14 (created that day, one commit); README read 2026-11-14. 2026-11-17: build v63e (2026-11-16) extends MOD GRAPHICS (gliding knob graphics) to the SYN pages of the stock machines by taking over the SYN page's draw method.

_Related: builds on `digikit` (README: derived from digikit (patched, pinned commit)); vendors `dn2-firmware-explore` (README: uses and ports code from dn2_firmware_explore; docs/js/dnfw is dnfw code unchanged) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### RIFT (second Digitone II firmware)

A second Digitone II firmware by the dn2mk2 author, separate from that mod: no Machinedrum or Monomachine machines, starting with one engine, FASCIA (two exciters into two coupled modal bodies, TZFM, ring and frequency shift, a spectral morph, a low-pass gate). Its first commit carries the dn2mk2 infrastructure (build framework, SHARC DSL, release gate); FASCIA's model, its float32 DSP-order contract and a bit-exact SHARC program come from dn2mk2 branches. Plan (docs/rift.md): stand FASCIA alone, measure its voice count, then integrate and release. The test bench is private. Found by find_new (new repo of a catalogued author) 2026-11-13. v0.1 (2026-11-13) removes the Machinedrum and Monomachine engines from the DSP image to fit the 2 MiB upgrade buffer. The roadmap (docs/rift-roadmap.md) plans per-track insert effects, an LPG filter type, a looping function-generator envelope and a granular machine. 2026-11-15 (releases/v0.3, ROADMAP): FASCIA fits about three voices of the heaviest patches and six to eight typical ones; sample voices get DSP time first. Planned next: an ORGAN engine, SILT, per-track insert effects, a granular sampler and stereo. 2026-11-17 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.4, docs/organ.md): v0.4 ORGAN ports the pipe organ of the author's Ravel firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1 (GPL-3.0) bit-exact to a float32 reference, then to the SHARC within a stated tolerance; it runs inside FASCIA's DSP program under the same guard and costs much less than a FASCIA voice. Known issue: FASCIA with BEND up and DAMP near 0 decays unevenly and sometimes cuts a voice (keep BEND at 10 or less). Next: SILT (material synthesis), the BEND fix, the reworked FLEX, then a bead engine and a Three Sisters-style filter. 2026-11-18 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.5-v0.6, docs/organ.md, docs/silt-dsp.md): v0.5 adds two ORGAN pages that leave v0.4's organ bit for bit at 0; v0.6 adds SILT (type 20) with a DSP cost plan: per-voice DDR delay lines, a 4-voice cap with the oldest voice stolen, graceful degradation of ensemble size, cost and stress gate steps with a negative control. Known issues in v0.6: v0.5 ORGAN sounds with MIXT up change (old PHRM/VELO values read as MTUN/MCHR); FIBER plays about twice as loud as the other materials. Planned: SILT level matching, CPU guardrails for every engine, LIGATURE (a modular voice wired by the user), the reworked FLEX. 2026-11-19 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.8): v0.7 takes FLEX buffers, MUTE SRC and the NAME screen over from dn2mk2 v0.54-v0.57; v0.8 brings back RESONATOR as machine type 22 (24 two-pole modes a voice, a mallet blended with a noise burst; notes ring through retriggers, a rung-out voice costs nothing, the newest notes are kept when time runs short). Next: a new screen style, LIGATURE and the first FX machines. 2026-11-20 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.9-v0.11): v0.9 removes RESONATOR again at the owner's decision (a v0.8 RESONATOR track opens as FM Tone), lists LIGATURE in MACHINE SEL and draws every RIFT machine on LINE pages (two rows of four moving glyphs, values shown the Syntakt way, locked cells inverted while their trig is held); a manual sits behind the patcher's MANUAL button. v0.10 puts DIGIDRUM on machine type 22, RESONATOR's old number, so a v0.8 RESONATOR track never re-saved in v0.9 opens as DIGIDRUM with its old values read as DIGIDRUM's. v0.11: the frame guard rendered voices newest first, so a melody or a re-struck note took the time and a held chord was stolen (a user report); now voices whose note is off go after every held voice. More held notes than the DSP can run still lose the oldest. Planned: THOLET (a piano leaning toward a Rhodes), a granular phase-vocoded looper in WERP's place, FX machines that other tracks feed, an own stretch algorithm. 2026-11-21 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.13-v0.14, docs/microtuning.md): v0.13 PARITY ports the DN2 mk2 mod's v0.60-v0.63 sampler updates (live slice edits, zero-crossing snap, GRID's ALLOCATE SLICE fix, a FLEX save that does not normalise, +24 dB on single-track FLEX takes, which the mod itself cut to +12 in its v0.65 after a tester's measurement: I185). v0.14 MONTUNE adds recorder MON, microtuning (every RIFT machine retunes; SLICE and GRID never; the same +Drive record region as the mod, not cleared by ERASE MOD DATA yet) and +12 dB playback for FLEX takes of MAIN and IN. Planned: THOLET, the granular looper, more LIGATURE blocks, and the mod's keyboard HOLD. 2026-11-22 (FIRMWARE.md, README, releases v0.15-v0.17, docs/smear.md, docs/tholet.md): v0.15 adds THOLET and the DN2 mk2 mod's KEYBOARD HOLD; the DSP upload then had 1.3 KB left of its 1 MiB. v0.16 SMEAR takes WERP's place (a saved WERP track opens as SMEAR with odd settings) with three readers of one loop: a phase vocoder, a tape-like read and eight grains. To make room the ColdFire sends ORGAN's, THOLET's and SMEAR's tables to the DSP at power-on, and those machines stay silent until the tables arrive. v0.16 also adds eight LIGATURE blocks and machine logos in MACHINE SEL. v0.17 PLATEAU is RIFT's first FX machine: a track fed by the sum of chosen tracks (the BUS page); only one plays at a time. THOLET is removed (its tracks open as FM Tone). All gated in the emulators, no unit result. The README now says "in development, released in small steps". 2026-11-23 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.18-v0.19, notices/2026-11-22-smear-plateau.md): a notice told users not to play SMEAR or PLATEAU on v0.16/v0.17: on the owner's and a tester's units a SMEAR note silenced every machine until a power cycle (I190). v0.18 turns SMEAR's vocoder off, makes the frame guard expect a voice's peak cost, replaces any non-finite or runaway block with silence, and prices every machine's worst block on a cost model of the unit (memory waits included) in the gate. It also adds GLASS, a filter type that a sound saved with it loads as Multi-Mode on stock or the DN2 mk2 mod. v0.19 adds CONTOUR, a wave-terrain synth whose idea comes from TERRAIN for the Digitone II (terrain-dn2); none of its code is used. The DSP image is 1,042,588 of 1,048,575 bytes. Power-cycle once after flashing: the first start can leave ORGAN silent. 2026-11-24 (v0.20, v0.21): a slide trig with no SLEN lock now lasts until the next trig, not one step (lock SLEN 1 for the old timing); a high CONTOUR note with feedback costs the DSP up to about four times more. v0.21's plate replaces the call of the stock reverb core and keeps sends, routing and LFO destinations; PLATEAU's 9 KB of DSP upload went to the plate. Takes a track recorded on earlier versions stay 18 dB hot (GAIN -18). Known: GLASS on several busy tracks can run the DSP past its frame and SMEAR's TUNE does nothing at BLND 0, both fixed in a gated v0.22 not yet released. 2026-11-25: owner reports from the unit drove v0.22/v0.23: GLASS on many busy tracks sounded crushed like a Monomachine overload (fifteen tracks cost 279k cycles over an idle frame of 415k), and FASCIA crackled on v0.21 even with one note because the guard dropped a lone voice. SMEAR VOC (phase vocoder) stays off since v0.18. Next planned: RUBBER filter, SPALL machine. 2026-11-26 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.24-v0.26, docs/smear.md): v0.24 replaces the GLASS filter with RUBBER, an SH-101-style four-pole ladder (zero-delay feedback, soft saturation, self-oscillation; sounds saved with GLASS open with RUBBER), and SMEAR now moves pitch and speed apart. v0.25 adds SPALL (machine type 26: tiny events on a stochastic clock rung through two resonators) and a DIN logo for the MIDI machine; on the way to the gate a test found SPALL's DSP routine labels duplicated SILT's, so a unit test now fails any label defined twice. v0.26 brings SMEAR's VOC back as a keyframe time stretch modelled on heavylight's Capicola and dt2-keyframer (credited, with permission; about 5,000 cycles a voice a block against 200,000-270,000 for the old phase vocoder), restores CONTOUR's original FDBK range, and fixes a user's report that RUBBER left a track silent: its DDR state was never cleared at power-on (I216). All three gated in the emulators (CLEARED TO FLASH), no unit result. 2026-11-27 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.27/v0.28, docs QA.md, inkey.md, midiarp.md, qa/LEDGER.md, qa/TAKEN-v0.27/v0.28): the DSP time guard now prices a voice at its last block x 1.25 and charges a higher floor only on the block that triggers it, after the old peak-on-every-block pricing left voices out with time free (I227, I228). Every release also gets an advisory review by a separate agent session against a frozen release branch; each finding is recorded as taken, deferred or declined, and a per-release ledger lists each machine's worst block on the cost model. The v0.28 gate was stopped and restarted after that review found two time floors set too low. The DSP program is nearly full (about 2 KB left in the 1 MiB program and about 800 bytes in the 2 MiB image), so DN2 mk2's PERFORM and extra project RAM banks do not fit. v0.27 takes the MIDI-track arp and in-key transpose code from upstream dnfw through DN2 mk2; those were tested on upstream's units, not on RIFT's. 2026-11-28 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.29.md, docs/qa/TAKEN-v0.28.md): v0.29 compiles out RUBBER's page code, adds a gate case that retriggers 16 ONESHOT voices together, and plays the whole loop for a project saved with SIZE above 120. Known: one report of FASCIA silent until its patch was cleared, not reproduced.

_Related: builds on `dn2mk2` (docs/rift.md: the infrastructure from dn2mk2-firmware e06993e (v0.51)); cites `terrain-dn2` (releases/v0.19: CONTOUR takes the idea of TERRAIN for the Digitone II; none of its code); cites `keyframer-lab` (releases/v0.26: SMEAR's VOC follows heavylight's keyframe time stretch (Capicola, dt2-keyframer), rewritten for RIFT); vendors `dn2-firmware-explore` (docs/midiarp.md, inkey.md (v0.27): MIDI-track arp, ARP OFS IN SCALE and degree transpose from upstream dnfw, by way of DN2 mk2) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### Digitone II mods (vitel2)

Four elekloader mods for the Digitone II, each its own .elemod, installed from the elekloader Mod Shop, which patches the user's own stock OS in the browser; all four can be combined and none needs another. MIDI LFO run fixes a stock 1.12 bug (SB31): after a new project, MIDI-track LFOs stop sending until a note trig plays on the track; with the mod FRE and TRG LFOs run without a trig, and their CCs stop while the transport is stopped (stock sends them then too). Its sites: lane update 0x40137770 and the LFO send loop's destination check 0x4012a340. The repo holds sources and thumbnails only, no firmware. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-19.

_Related: mod for `elekloader` (README: elekloader mods installed from the elekloader Mod Shop) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-19, README (2026-11-19)_

### DigiGlide

A Digitone II firmware mod in which a track holds a chord and its voices glide into the next chord along shaped paths; a port of the author's Brickglide engine (from his brickchord project) to FM TONE, WAVETONE, FM DRUM and SWARMER tracks, as four extra pages after the machine's SYN pages. A Python patcher (no packages) builds the image from the user's own official OS 1.12 file and writes it only if the result matches the tested image byte for byte; install with Elektron Transfer. The README gives the DIN MIDI recovery (FUNC + TRIG 4 at power-on, about 12-15 minutes) and ships no Elektron firmware. 26 commits, all by the author; created 2026-11-13. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-22. 2026-11-23: listed by altstrument (beta-35, patch-your-own, no brick-risk flag).

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-22, README, NOTICE (2026-11-22), altstrument directory entry (2026-11-23)_

### Multitone (shared multi-boot kernel design for Digitone II firmwares)

A design, not built: a small boot kernel that could start a Digitone II firmware kept on the +Drive instead of the one in flash and fall back to a safe one when that fails, plus one shared rule for the extra data each custom firmware keeps (+Drive sector ranges, RAM ranges, machine-type numbers), its identity (number, 4-letter id, brand, name, version) and how projects made with another firmware are recognised. A proposed registry gives stock DN2 machine types 0..17 and the +Drive slot store 0x000000..0x5D7FFF, and reserves +Drive 0x5FFE00..0x5FFFFF and RAM 0x476F8000..0x47700000 and 0x47800000..0x47FFFFFF for the kernel; address tables per stock version (1.12 first), switched off on others. Nothing has run on a unit or in an emulator; open questions Q1-Q8. One commit, 2026-11-22. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-23.

_Related: cites `dn2-wishes` (registry/firmwares.txt: Wishes holds machine types 50..62 and its +Drive and RAM ranges in the proposal) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-23, README, registry/firmwares.txt (2026-11-23)_

### DN2 WISHES

A Digitone II OS 1.12 firmware built on the dn2mk2 mod (a GitHub fork of De-Pattern's dn2mk2-firmware with about 300 commits of its own since it branched; the history also carries upstream's and dn2-firmware-explore's). Its own machines are types 50-56 in MACHINE SEL: JUNO (a Juno-106 voice), ANALOG (two oscillators, five filter models), DRONE, SOPHIE, TB-303 (Open303), PLAITS and DRUM; paraphonic mode on ANALOG and JUNO; insert effects (FUZZ, TAPE, FOLD, CHOR, WIDE, HARM, FDN8, XDLY, SUB, DIST, GATER, RING, JUNO); a modulation matrix; a voice budget that takes an old note's voice before the DSP runs out of time. The machines ported from the Monomachine, Machinedrum and Digitakt II come from dn2mk2. A browser builder makes the image from the user's own Elektron files and flashes it over USB; a build may be flashed only after the ship gate prints CLEARED TO FLASH (bootstrap and updater stock byte for byte, both processors emulated, stock audio compared bit for bit). Proposes the Multitone shared multi-boot rule (multitone). Found as a new repo of a catalogued author 2026-11-23. 2026-11-24 (CHANGELOG): three test builds, none installed on a unit: v0.69.2-dualboot keeps a copy of stock 1.12's DSP program on the +Drive (sent once over USB, checked sector by sector) so SAFE MODE can play with the stock sound; v0.69.2-fdn8hw runs FDN8's loops as the DSP's hardware loops (about 4 % less per bus FDN8 in the emulator, bit-identical sound); v0.69.2-all combines both, gives each DT2 sample machine its own icon and counts the notes, voices and inserts the guard left out. Offered as a hidden TEST entry on the builder.

_Related: fork of `dn2mk2` (GitHub fork; README: built on dn2mk2 by De-Pattern) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-23, README, CHANGELOG, VERSION, LICENSE, about page source (2026-11-23), CHANGELOG, README (2026-11-24)_
